messages:
lucas-runtime: Quick heads-up — did an "envelope" sweep where we blend NTK+linear RoPE scaling (weights vary per-layer) and enable the YARN damping fallback on the long-ctx path. Target models: Mistral-7B-v0, Mixtral-8x7B-lite, and Qwen-7B. Ran with both our default kernel-router and a forced kernel pin to fused_gemm_v2.

ajay-ml: Nice. High-level numbers?

lucas-runtime: Short summary: forced kernel (fused_gemm_v2) reduces cross-kernel memcpy by ~30% in our trace, p50 token latency down ~8–10% on batching=auto. But: when we use the NTK:linear blend where NTK_ratio > 0.6, Qwen shows a small perplexity bump on the 8k eval set (+2.1 PPL), and Mixtral exhibits occasional KV cache inconsistency under heavy concurrent KV handoff (seen as token duplication).

maria-ops: Oof token duplication — reproducible? could be a race in kv-shard handoff logic? Any logs?

lucas-runtime: Repro steps included — ran the microbench harness with 256 concurrent requests, short prompt bursts + long completion tails. Relevant command run:```bash
./bench/run_rope_env.sh \
  --models "mistral-7b,mixtral-8x7b,qwen-7b" \
  --rope-mix "ntk:0.7,line:0.3" \
  --kv-handoff enabled \
  --kernel-policy auto|pin:fused_gemm_v2 \
  --ctx 8192 \
  --concurrency 256
```
Attached log excerpt:```
[run] model=mixtral-8x7b worker=3 handoff=start seq=1024
[cache] shard=5 state=handoff pending=2
[emit] seq=1024 token=\"the\"
[emit] seq=1024 token=\"the\"  # duplicate observed
```

carol-eng: Handoff race sounds like our transition path doesn't atomically swap kv pointers when multiple threads flush a prefix cache. Could be exacerbated by kernel switching — more context switches means the window increases.

ajay-ml: On the PPL regression for Qwen: is it correlated with layers that have odd head/kv dim ratios? We saw similar before when RoPE scaling changed relative to head dim (NTK interacts poorly with certain rotary bases).

lucas-runtime: Good catch — per-layer breakdown shows the biggest PPL deltas concentrated in layers 2/5/21 for Qwen (heads 32, kv-dim 128). Might be numerical amplification from the mixed RoPE schedules. Also observed more attention score saturation in those layers.

maria-ops: Any perf-regression vs baseline when kernel pinned? You said latency improved but did tail variance change?

lucas-runtime: Tail (p95/p99) improved for Mistral when pinned; Mixtral p95 is stable; Qwen p99 saw a tiny bump (~4%) but only when we combine kv-handoff=enabled + rope-mix where NTK_ratio >= 0.7. Hypothesis: kernel pin eliminates extra memcpy but forces a codepath with slightly different floating point ordering (different fused kernels), exposing numerical edge cases given aggressive RoPE scaling.

perf-bot: CI perf suite results summary: model:mistral-7b p50 -9.2% (pin), p99 -5.1% ; model:qwen-7b p50 -3.4% (pin), p99 +4.1% (pin + ntk-heavy).

carol-eng: Actionable items: (1) Add an atomic handoff in kv cache swap (simple CAS) and add a unit test that spawns multiple flushers. (2) Add a toggle to avoid kernel pin for Qwen when ntk_ratio > 0.6 by default (fallback policy). (3) Run a high-precision run (fp32 deterministic) for the Qwen layers that showed PPL spikes to confirm numeric source.

ajay-ml: I'll take (3) and reproduce the PPL delta with deterministic seeds. Also will run an ablation: pure-NTK vs pure-linear vs blended with ratios [0.25,0.5,0.75] to map safe envelope per-model.

maria-ops: I'll scope the rollback control — create a routing policy that disables kernel pin per-customer or per-model label. If we detect >1% quality drift on eval set, auto-disable kernel pin and route to compatible kernels.

lucas-runtime: I'll prototype the CAS-based kv swap and add a small microbenchmark for handoff latency. Also will instrument kernel-router to emit a tag when it switches kernels mid-request (so we can correlate with dupes).

carol-eng: Test matrix itemization (short):
- deterministic fp32 Qwen longctx 8k (ablations)
- kv-handoff stress: concurrency [64,128,256,512] on Mixtral pinned/unpinned
- kernel-router telemetry: map kernel change events -> duplicate/emit anomalies

ajay-ml: Quick note: if we find numeric amplification, consider reducing NTK scaling near low-head dims or mapping a per-head scale clamp. Might be safer than fully disabling NTK for Qwen.

maria-ops: Scheduling: can we run the full sweep on staging GPUs tonight? We have a slot at 0200 UTC. I'll schedule and post reservation.

lucas-runtime: Thanks. I'll push the kv fix PR and add logs before the run. If anyone wants to look at the raw traces, I'll drop them in the thread after the run. :mag: :gear:
